children: M&G shares declined after the U.K. investment manager said it expected adjusted profit growth to slow, as it recorded a hit of 325 million pounds ($438.3 million) due to the U.K. government's cap on existing ground rents.
Shares fell 1.7% to 337.22 pence during early morning European trading. However, the stock has climbed 16% year to date.

M&G said Thursday that it swung to a loss of 170 million pounds for the first half of 2026 from a 243 million pound profit a year prior. The company said this was impacted by 551 million pounds in negative short-term fluctuations in investment returns, of which 325 million pounds related to the write-down on U.K. ground rent assets.

Earlier this year the U.K. government capped ground rents-- which are payments made by the holder of a leasehold property to the land owner--at 250 pounds a year. M&G previously said it holds 722 million pounds of ground rent assets, based on June 2025 figures.
Excluding the write-down, adjusted operating pretax profit grew 15% to 435 million pounds, ahead of the company-compiled consensus of 429 million pounds.

Looking ahead, M&G guided to low double-digit adjusted pretax operating profit growth in 2026, suggesting a slowdown from the 15% rise in the first half. The company said it is committed to average annual growth in adjusted pretax operating profit of at least 5% between 2025 and 2027.

Net flows from open business reached 2.4 billion pounds in the first half, up from 2.1 billion pounds. Assets under management and administration increased to 387 billion pounds from 355 billion pounds a year ago.
M&G raised its interim dividend to 6.8 pence per share from 6.7 pence a year ago, in line with expectations.

title: M&G Shares Fall on Lower Profit Growth Outlook
